elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall...", covering both trigger events for both the assistance and export limbs.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The insertion commits Licensor to assistance "for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; there is no six-month duration anywhere in the operative text. To reach preferred, change the period to up to six (6) months.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis appears in the inserted paragraph; the drafter expressly omitted the then-current-rates mechanic. Add "at Licensor's then-current rates" to meet this element.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall, within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Licensee all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee that is in Licensor's possession or control."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The export obligation specifies no format; add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the delivery limb.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or certification obligation is imposed on Licensor (the only certificate in Article XXI runs from an officer of Licensee for Licensor's materials). Add a post-return deletion-and-written-certification limb.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason" governs both the 90-day assistance and the 30-day export; the request condition is not limited to anticipated expiry, so it applies after every covered ending.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall, at Licensee's request, provide transition assistance to Licensee for a period of at least ninety (90) days" — Vendor-side obligation, minimum 90 days.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Licensee all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee that is in Licensor's possession or control" — deadline runs from termination, not from a request, and the data scope covers every category of Licensee data.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Not an element of the fallback checklist; the fallback requires only assistance and export, so its absence does not defeat fallback completeness.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (expiry-or-termination trigger, at least 90 days of Licensor assistance, and export/delivery of all Licensee data within 30 days of expiry or termination).

Preferred is incomplete on four elements: six-month duration, then-current rates, machine-readable format, and post-return certified deletion. If the drafter wants preferred, amend the period to "up to six (6) months", add "at Licensor's then-current rates", add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export limb, and add a limb requiring Licensor to delete Licensee data thereafter and certify deletion in writing.

Minimality holds: the finding is a true gap (Article XXI is one-way and contains no Licensor-side exit mechanics), the insertion is a single concise paragraph confined to the two fallback mechanics, and no words were deleted or paraphrased outside the target elements. No survival tail, expense allocation, damages, or procedural boilerplate was added.

Intent is preserved: Article XXI's existing obligations (licence termination, Licensee's five-day return of Licensed Technology and Confidential Information with an officer's certificate) survive unchanged, and the retained sentence that Licensor's rights survive termination does not contradict a newly imposed Licensor obligation. No undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created; the insertion self-describes the data scope rather than relying on an undefined "Customer Data" definition.
Deterministic checks (operation applies, transition/data-return present, minimality gate, element coverage gate) all pass and are borne out on substantive reading of the rendered text.
